F. Scott Fitzgerald, The Great Gatsby.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/f-scott-fitzgerald/the-great-gatsby

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- F. Scott Fitzgerald, the author, died 1940.

First publication of the text used: 1925 (SE colophon: 'The Great Gatsby was published in 1925 by F. Scott Fitzgerald'). Wikipedia's article on the novel gives the country as the United States and the publisher as Charles Scribner's Sons (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_Gatsby).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in the United States in 1925, before 1931. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it on 1 January 2021.
- Country of origin (United States): the country of origin is the United States, so the United States rule above also settles the country of origin. The last person to die among those whose words are in the text died in 1940 (Wikidata Q93354, P570 = 1940-12-21).

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
